title: Conegliano Valdobbiadene
subtitle: Prosecco's hills
objectives: Explain why the hills give better wines

steps.title: The DOCG
steps.body: Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore DOCG lies in the steep hills between the towns of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene, north of Venice. The hills, called hogbacks, are so steep that most work is by hand. The area became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019. Asolo, nearby, is a second DOCG.

steps.title: Rive and Cartizze
steps.body: Rive are single-village or hamlet crus on the steepest slopes, 43 in total, picked by hand with lower yields. Cartizze, a single hill of about 107 hectares near Valdobbiadene, is the most prized, with some of Italy's most expensive vineyard land. Its wines are traditionally a little sweeter, often labelled Dry.

options: A prized single hill in Valdobbiadene
steps.explanation: Cartizze is Prosecco's top cru, about 107 hectares.

steps.title: Why the hills
steps.body: Hillside vineyards drain well, get more sun and cooler nights than the plains, and have lower yields. The wines are more aromatic, more complex and more mineral. Some producers in the hills also make Col Fondo, a traditional style refermented in bottle and left unfiltered, cloudy with lees.

steps.prompt: The Conegliano Valdobbiadene hills are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Conegliano Valdobbiadene DOCG is Prosecco's hill heartland
Rive and Cartizze are its top crus
Col Fondo is a traditional, bottle-fermented style
